findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, exposing long-lived IAM credentials to anyone with EC2 console/API access, instance metadata access, or access to Terraform state.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force attacks.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0. Combined with public subnet placement and no TLS configuration, this exposes the web server broadly and traffic is served in cleartext.

The security group allows all outbound traffic (all ports/protocols) to 0.0.0.0/0, violating least privilege and facilitating data exfiltration or command-and-control communication if the instance is compromised.

map_public_ip_on_launch is enabled, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet (including the internet-facing portal_server), increasing the internet-facing attack surface.

map_public_ip_on_launch is enabled, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, expanding the internet-facing attack surface even though the subnet is otherwise unused by compute in this file.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data at rest on the attached disk is unencrypted, violating encryption-at-rest requirements.

The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving potentially sensitive network flow data unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block / bucket policy
findings.description: No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy restricting access is defined for the bucket storing flow logs, leaving it reliant on account-level defaults and potentially exposed to public or unintended access.
